conclusions.question: What was properties.authConfig before the test?
How does Learn enable Entra ID, does it work, and how long does it take to apply?
conclusions.answer: Learn's CLI pivot uses `az documentdb mongocluster update --name <cluster> --resource-group <rg> --auth-allowed-modes NativeAuth MicrosoftEntraID`. The documentdb extension 1.0.0 has that flag (allowed values NativeAuth, MicrosoftEntraID), so no az rest PATCH was needed. The command exited 0 after 155.4 s with no stderr. The body it returned already had allowedModes [MicrosoftEntraID, NativeAuth] but still showed provisioningState and clusterStatus 'Updating'. A show 0.6 s later reported Succeeded and Ready. The service stores the list as ["MicrosoftEntraID", "NativeAuth"], and native SCRAM logins kept working.

conclusions.question: Does enabling Entra change what hello advertises?
conclusions.answer: Yes. hello.saslSupportedMechs changes from ['SCRAM-SHA-256'] to ['MONGODB-OIDC', 'SCRAM-SHA-256'], and the same list comes back for every user string, registered or not. Before the change the managed service matched open-source 1.2.0, which always returns ['SCRAM-SHA-256'].

conclusions.question: Which CLI command manages Entra users on the cluster, and what values does --type accept?
conclusions.answer: `az documentdb mongocluster microsoft-entra-user` (assign, list, remove, show, wait); the other subgroups (firewall-rule, identity, replica) do not manage Entra users. From assign --help, verbatim: "--type -t : The Microsoft Entra principal type of the user. Allowed values: User, ServicePrincipal. Example: --type User.  Allowed values: ServicePrincipal, User." There is no managed-identity value. --object-id is still described as "Object ID (client ID) of the Microsoft Entra principal. Provide the GUID of the service principal or user, not a friendly name or UPN." This matches DECISIONS topic 5.

conclusions.question: Can the signed-in personal Microsoft account be registered as an administrative Entra identity?
conclusions.answer: Yes. The account is a personal Microsoft account (token idp live.com) that is a Member of its own directory (UPN carries #EXT#, identity issuer MicrosoftAccount); it is not a B2B guest. `az documentdb mongocluster microsoft-entra-user assign --object-id <object-id> --cluster-name ddb-samples-shared --resource-group documentdb-samples-rg --type User --role db=admin role=root` succeeded in 63.6 s (users/<object-id>, principalType User, roles [{db: admin, role: root}], provisioningState Succeeded). The first OIDC connection, 8 s after the command returned, authenticated. A B2B guest from another tenant, a service principal and a managed identity were not tested.

conclusions.question: What does the service return for MONGODB-OIDC at each stage?
conclusions.answer: NativeAuth only: code 18 AuthenticationFailed "The authentication mechanism provided is not supported in the service.". Entra enabled, principal not registered: code 18 AuthenticationFailed "External identity is not present in the system.". saslStart with no JWT (an empty or principal-only payload) on an Entra-enabled cluster: code 18 AuthenticationFailed "JWT token missing from OIDC payload". No server reply carried errorLabels; the Node driver adds HandshakeError and ResetPool on the client side. Open-source 1.2.0 answers MONGODB-OIDC with code 18 "'MONGODB-OIDC' is not a supported authentication scheme.", so the code is the same and every message differs.

conclusions.question: Which PyMongo versions connect with Learn's Python OIDC callback (AzureCliCredential token for https://ossrdbms-aad.database.windows.net/.default, plain host, tls=True, retryWrites=False)?
conclusions.answer: 4.6.3 cannot authenticate at all. `from pymongo.auth_oidc import OIDCCallback` raises ImportError, and a callback object under OIDC_CALLBACK raises ValueError "Auth mechanism property values must be strings or callback functions". Its undocumented pre-GA request_token_callback is refused for the Azure host by the default allowed_hosts; with allowed_hosts set, it fails inside the driver with KeyError 'MONGODB-OIDC'. 4.7.0 fails with Learn's code as written: ConfigurationError "Refusing to connect to fc-a472369cc681-000.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com, which is not in authOIDCAllowedHosts: [...]" is raised before the callback runs. With ALLOWED_HOSTS ['*.azure.com'] or ['*.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com'], 4.7.0 connects and ping, find and insert work. 4.10.1 still refuses. 4.11 and 4.20.2 (latest) connect with no ALLOWED_HOSTS, on both the plain and .global. hosts. The source of every release checked from 4.7.0 to 4.10.1 (4.7.0-4.7.3, 4.8.0, 4.9.0-4.9.2, 4.10.0, 4.10.1) checks ALLOWED_HOSTS for any credential without ENVIRONMENT. 4.11, 4.11.3, 4.12.0, 4.13.0 and 4.20.2 check it only for human callbacks. So 4.7 is the MONGODB-OIDC floor only if ALLOWED_HOSTS is set, and Learn's sample as written needs 4.11 or later. This corrects the DECISIONS topic 5 line saying pymongo checks ALLOWED_HOSTS only for human callbacks: that is true only from 4.11.

conclusions.question: Which Node.js driver versions connect with Learn's OIDC_CALLBACK, and which ALLOWED_HOSTS pattern works?
conclusions.answer: 6.6.0 does not connect. The constructor throws MongoInvalidArgumentError "Either a PROVIDER_NAME or a REQUEST_TOKEN_CALLBACK must be specified for mechanism 'MONGODB-OIDC'." with ['*.azure.com'], with ['*.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com'] and with no ALLOWED_HOSTS. Its pre-GA REQUEST_TOKEN_CALLBACK gets server code 18 "JWT token missing from OIDC payload". 6.7.0 and 7.9.1 (latest) connect, ping and find with both ['*.azure.com'] (Learn) and ['*.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com'] (MCP); the narrow pattern also matches through the .global. host. Without ALLOWED_HOSTS, both refuse on the client side and never call the callback. 6.7.0 raises MongoInvalidArgumentError "Host 'fc-a472369cc681-000.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com:10260' is not valid for OIDC authentication with ALLOWED_HOSTS of '*.mongodb.net,*.mongodb-qa.net,*.mongodb-dev.net,*.mongodbgov.net,localhost,127.0.0.1,::1'". 7.9.1 raises the same error with ',*.mongo.com' appended to the list; neither default list has an Azure domain. This matches DECISIONS 4.2 (floor 6.7.0) and the topic 5 ALLOWED_HOSTS item.

conclusions.question: Does Learn's TypeScript expiresInSeconds bug break the connection?
conclusions.answer: No visible effect. With Learn's formula, expiresInSeconds came out as 1793854691680, and both 6.7.0 and 7.9.1 still connected, pinged and found. This matches DECISIONS topic 5 ('runtime impact nil').

conclusions.question: What do connectionStatus with showPrivileges and usersInfo return for the Entra administrator?
conclusions.answer: connectionStatus returns authenticatedUsers [{user: '<object-id>', db: 'admin'}] and authenticatedUserRoles [{role: 'root', db: 'admin'}]; with showPrivileges it adds three privilege entries (db ''/collection '', cluster, admin db). usersInfo '<object-id>' (run on admin, or on the $external database) returns _id 'admin.<object-id>', db 'admin', roles [root@admin] and customData.IdentityProvider {type: 'MicrosoftEntraID', properties: {principalType: 'user'}}; showPrivileges adds inheritedPrivileges. usersInfo {user: '<object-id>', db: '$external'} fails with code 2 BadValue "Unsupported value specified for 'db' field. Only 'admin' is allowed.". usersInfo: 1 lists the Entra administrator and factoryadmin. Results were the same on PyMongo 4.7.0 (with ALLOWED_HOSTS) and 4.20.2. This identity is root, so the DECISIONS question about non-admin callers stays open.

conclusions.question: How is an Entra administrator represented across the surfaces?
conclusions.answer: In the database, the user name is the object id in db admin, not $external, although drivers run the SASL conversation against $external. In ARM it is users/<object-id> with identityProvider.type MicrosoftEntraID and principalType 'User'; the database customData has 'user' in lower case. The ARM REST GET (api-version 2026-06-01) also returns properties.user and identityProvider.properties.entraTenant (the tenant id), and the CLI output leaves both out. The native admin is listed as users/factoryadmin with no identityProvider.

conclusions.question: Do the connection strings change when Entra is enabled?
conclusions.answer: list-connection-strings gains two strings without credentials: GlobalMicrosoftEntraId (mongodb+srv://ddb-samples-shared.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com/?tls=true&authMechanism=MONGODB-OIDC&retrywrites=false&maxIdleTimeMS=120000) and MicrosoftEntraId (the same on the plain host). properties.connectionString stays the SCRAM-SHA-256 string.

conclusions.question: Does the service support the two-step OIDC human flow (server returns IdP info first)?
conclusions.answer: No sign of it. Every saslStart without a token got code 18 "JWT token missing from OIDC payload" rather than IdP information, so only the one-step JWT flow (machine or custom callback) works. Human flows that need the server's IdP info (OIDC_HUMAN_CALLBACK, PyMongo human_callback, the pre-GA two-step APIs) should fail. No human callback was actually run.

conclusions.question: DECISIONS 4.12-open: does the service accept MONGODB-OIDC from these drivers on a given compatibility version?
conclusions.answer: Yes on serverVersion 8.0 (wire version 25, engine 2.2-1/2.3.0) with PyMongo 4.7.0+ (with ALLOWED_HOSTS), 4.11+ (without), and Node 6.7.0 and 7.9.1. Versions 5.0, 6.0 and 7.0 were not tested.
